result:
I found where the DOA2U fight's `surface_update` time goes and pushed a fix for it, but it isn't measured on the device yet. PR #440 stays in draft until those results are back.

**Why attempts 1 and 2 didn't finish:** both ended while the pilot soak was still queued, and neither posted a `waiting:` comment. The pilot has since run and is valid: the `[surf413]` probe printed 111 lines, and the fight ran at 11–15 fps. Attempt 3's reasons are recorded in `docs/lanes/doa413b/NOTES.md`.

**Where the time goes:** in the fight, `Surf` is 61–63 ms per frame, and 51–59 ms of that is one wait. The first `surface_update` of each frame calls `pgraph_vk_download_surface_complete_deferred()`, which waits for the GPU to finish the whole previous frame. So the CPU and GPU never work at the same time. Lookup, bind, upload and expire together cost under 0.4 ms per frame, and none of the four causes I'd guessed from the code held up against the numbers.

**The fix (7f01f7f157, in `vk/surface.c`):** that per-frame wait is removed, and whatever next reads the affected video memory finishes the pending copy first. Two things come with it:
- It is on by default; setting `XEMU_SURF_LAZY_COMPLETE=0` restores the old behaviour.
- Every build now prints a `[lazy413]` counter line every 5 s, so a test run can show the new path actually ran.

The GPU alone takes 40–48 ms per frame in this fight, so expect roughly 20–24 fps, not 30. It compiles with no errors on Android, both with and without the perf logging. There is no desktop build on this host, so the desktop build is untested. `preflight.sh` passes.

**Waiting on three device results, all on the Nova:**
- Soak `1790461490-doa413b-542947`: new path off.
- Soak `1790461494-doa413b-546424`: new path on, same APK as the other soak.
- The graphics-test regression check, registered in `docs/testing/predictions/doa413b-lazy-mnm.json` (0d5f93f210 vs 7f01f7f157), which should come back as a verdict on the PR.

About 115 queue entries are ahead of the soaks and the Nova has a hold on it, so this will take hours. I posted the `[lane.doa413b] waiting:` comment on #440, and the PR body lists the files and prediction. If the regression check fails, the next step is to make the new path off by default and say so in the PR.

The host still needs to run its dispatcher update window before the `xemu-surf:I` logcat change in `docs/testing/dispatcher.sh` takes effect.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in claude.ai's connector settings before they can be used; this lane didn't need them.
